summary: Elevated TTFB for chat on small payloads after runtime variant swap
description:
Issue summary: Customer reports sudden increase in time-to-first-token (TTFB) specifically for short chat prompts (<= 40 tokens) after a runtime variant swap that rolled out earlier the same day. Impact: customer-facing chat experiences show 600-1500ms additional delay before first token; long-form prompts unaffected. Environment: prod (us-east-1) using dedicated enterprise tenancy for BrightRoute AI. Observed start: approx 2026-03-10 08:10 UTC, coincident with runtime variant swap between v1.11 -> v1.12 that included a kernel selection heuristic and quantized-variant routing update.

Notes: This ticket tracks the customer-facing support thread; engineering is parallel-tracking in INT-8123. Customer requests workaround or rollback to avoid user-visible degradation for high-volume short prompts.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Send a chat completion request with a short prompt (6-30 tokens) to the customer's workspace in prod (us-east-1).
2) Observe TTFB measured at client side (round-trip to first token).
3) Compare with sending a long prompt (200+ tokens) to same model and environment; long prompt shows expected TTFB.
4) Toggle model pin to runtime-v1.11 to confirm regression reverts.

comments: 2026-03-10 08:20 - BrightRoute Support: Noticed all short prompts are slow; long ones look fine. Can you confirm any rollout today?
2026-03-10 08:25 - Maya Chen (Support): We see a runtime variant swap starting at ~08:10 UTC. Looping in infra/serving-runtime. INT-8123 created for engineering investigation.

2026-03-10 09:00 - Diego Alvarez (Eng): Early hypothesis: new kernel-selection heuristics are routing short sequences to quantized variant which triggers a just-in-time compile on some nodes. Collecting traces and compile latencies.

2026-03-11 11:40 - BrightRoute Support: Workaround applied (pin to runtime-v1.11) seems to drop TTFB back to baseline; requesting confirmation of root cause and whether a platform-side fix will be applied.

2026-03-12 15:10 - Diego Alvarez (Eng): Confirmed non-deterministic JIT compile path for small sequences on some nodes; patch PR opened to bypass JIT for precompiled quant-kernel bundle. ETA for staged rollout: 2026-03-13.
investigation_notes: Collected flamegraphs from node-gpu-12: majority of extra latency attributed to 'kernel compile' and 'linking' phases when runtime_variant=v1.12 and kernel=quant-kernel-v3.
Router logs show heuristic: if avg_sequence_length < 48 and model flagged as quantized-capable -> route to quantized-variant. This changed in v1.12 to prefer quantized path aggressively.

Observed that small payloads trigger continuous-batching threshold behavior: waiting briefly for batch fill when fast-path would be faster; combined with occasional JIT compile causes amplified TTFB for low-latency short prompts.
Correlation: customers with high proportion of small prompts and lower per-tenant warm cache saw highest impact. BrightRoute uses many short prompts (search/snippet style).
Reproduced locally by sending 500 short requests; ~18% landed on nodes that performed JIT compile on first occurrence, causing a bimodal TTFB distribution.
workaround: Customer pinned their workspace to runtime-v1.11 and enabled 'prompt-prefetch' which forces warmup of KV cache. This reduced observed TTFB to baseline for short prompts.
resolution: In progress - engineering deployed a hotfix on a subset of nodes that disables JIT compile for quant-kernel-v3 when routing short sequences. Customer remains pinned until full rollout completes.
resolution_notes: Hotfix patch (PR #7892) adds a precompiled kernel bundle for quant-kernel-v3 and changes router to prefer fastpath for sequences < 32 tokens for enterprise tenancies with strict latency SLOs. Staged rollout started 2026-03-12; monitoring for regression metrics. Full rollback option available if new issues detected.
root_cause: Aggressive kernel-selection heuristic introduced in runtime v1.12 routed short-sequence traffic to a quantized kernel that triggered JIT/compile steps on cold nodes, and combined with micro-batching wait heuristics produced elevated TTFB for small prompts.
followups: Postmortem write-up in Confluence with timeline and measurements (owner: Diego Alvarez).
Add guardrail to rollout process to run short-prompt latency smoke tests when changing kernel-selection heuristics.
Add metric: percent of short-seq requests that hit JIT-compile path (alert if > 1% over 10m).
